MR JUSTICE M.G.S. KAMAL

ORAL ORDER Petitioners are before this Court claiming to be the owners of land bearing Sy.No.29/1 measuring 3 acres situated at Burudaghatta Village, Kora Hobli, Tumakuru District, of which 18 guntas of land was acquired by the respondent authorities for the purpose of Yettinahole project.
2. The case of the petitioners is that the nature of the land was changed from agricultural to non-agricultural residential purpose in terms of order dated 18.02.2011, NC: 2025:KHC:940 issued by office of Deputy Commissioner as per Annexure- C.

However, as per the award passed vide Annexure-K, respondent authorities have assessed the compensation taking the nature of the land as agricultural land, which has caused substantial loss and hardship to the petitioners.
3. That apart it is the case of the petitioners that since Yettinahole project is running through and cutting across the land of petitioners, the utilization/utility of the land has been reduced.

Therefore,
petitioners are seeking allotment of alternate land.

In furtherance whereof, petitioners have made representation dated 09.01.2019 and 26.08.2020 as per Annexure-G and J seeking allotment of alternate land, compensation of which has constrained the petitioners to dispossess.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners on instructions submits that as regards enhancement of Pramod R Kamath vs State Of Karnataka on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42207517/
2 compensation is concerned, they be reserved liberty to approach the concerned authority in terms of the NC: 2025:KHC:940 provisions of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: Thus, learned counsel further submits that petitioners would restrict their petition only to the extent of their prayer for allotment of alternate land and also submits that respondent authorities be directed to consider their representation to the extent of grant or allotment of alternate land.
Submission is taken on record.

5. Learned Additional Government Advocate and learned counsel appearing for respondent beneficiary submits that since counsel for the petitioners has submitted that their case regarding enhancement of compensation would be resorted to in terms of provisions of the Act, they would consider the request for allotment of alternate land, if permissible under law.
Submission is taken on record.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER (i) Respondent authorities to consider, if there is provisions for allotment of alternate land NC: 2025:KHC:940 as sought for by the petitioners, same shall be considered in accordance with law and order in this regard one way or the other be passed and be communicated to the petitioners as expeditiously as possible.
(ii) Writ petition is disposed of accordingly.

SD/-
